title: GRPO Hands-On: Teaching a Small Model to Reason with Verifiable Rewards
summary: Train a small instruct model with GRPO on GSM8K maths problems on a free Colab T4: write reward functions that cannot be gamed, configure TRL's GRPOTrainer with LoRA, do the memory and time arithmetic before you run, and read the logged signals to tell learning from collapse or reward hacking.
objectives: Compute group-relative advantages, the clipped ratio term and the KL estimator for a worked group, and map each to the TRL argument and the from-scratch code in part_9
Write correctness, format and length reward functions in TRL's signature and guard them against common reward hacks
Configure GRPOConfig so the batch divides into groups and the run fits a 15 GB T4, and estimate its memory and step time
Diagnose a run from reward, reward_std, frac_reward_zero_std, completion length, KL and entropy, and evaluate with greedy accuracy and pass@k on a held-out set
prerequisites: The GRPO idea from [Verifiable rewards and group-relative advantages](/learn/fine-tuning/preference-tuning/verifiable-rewards-grpo) and PPO's clipped objective from [RLHF with PPO](/learn/fine-tuning/preference-tuning/rlhf-ppo). A working notebook environment from [Run fine-tuning yourself](/learn/fine-tuning/run-fine-tuning-yourself), LoRA from [LoRA and QLoRA](/learn/fine-tuning/peft-lora), and where GRPO sits among DPO-style methods from [Preference optimization methods](/learn/fine-tuning/preference-optimization-methods).
